title: Deterministic workflow versus model-directed agent
summary: Show who chooses the next action and who may perform it.

claims.text: Anthropic distinguishes predefined workflow paths from agents that choose processes and tool use dynamically.

levels.overview: Contrast a known checklist with an open-ended investigation.
levels.architecture: Compare chain, routing, parallel work and an evaluator loop with explicit stop conditions.
levels.detail: Inspect permitted tools, step attempts, review gates, handoffs and observed results.

example.input: A synthetic request needs a summary, a check and an owner decision.
steps: Ask for the decision at the existing gate.
example.output: A bounded workflow; autonomous delegation remains a separate option.
limits: No agents are launched by a lesson.
Provider roles are illustrative, not live session ownership.

alternatives.label: Model-directed loop
alternatives.whenToConsider: Consider when evaluated flexibility justifies additional uncertainty and cost.

interview.question: What makes a workflow agentic, and when would you avoid adding autonomy?
answerHints: Measure usefulness rather than number of agents.

instanceMappingPolicy: An explicit source-pinned link is required; names, icons and tags are not evidence.
